binders: Universally quantify an arbitrary function p=profile : ℝ → ℝ and an arbitrary constant c=speed ∈ ℝ.
Define q(x,t)=p(x−ct); x is the spatial argument and t the temporal argument.
In the first clause, universally quantify x∈ℝ. In each of the second and third clauses, universally quantify x,t∈ℝ independently.
In the third clause, τ∈ℝ is the variable of the function being differentiated, while x is fixed and t is the derivative evaluation point.

In the fourth clause, after assuming p differentiable everywhere, universally quantify x,t∈ℝ and then existentially quantify qt,qx∈ℝ. These witnesses may depend on p,c,x,t; the quantifier for qx is inside that for qt.
In the fifth clause's antecedent, universally quantify interval endpoints a,b∈ℝ.

In the fifth clause's conclusion, universally quantify a,b,t for spatial integrability, x,s,t for temporal flux integrability, and a,b,s,t for the balance identity. Integration variables are bound separately.
The flux is the fixed function F : ℝ → ℝ defined by F(state)=c·state; state is its bound real argument.
hypotheses: There are no regularity or sign assumptions on p or c for the first three clauses.
Only the fourth clause assumes that p is differentiable over ℝ at every real point.
Only the fifth clause assumes that p is interval integrable with respect to μ for every pair of real endpoints a,b, where μ is the volume measure selected by Real.measureSpace.
The differentiability and interval-integrability assumptions belong to separate implications; neither is an additional hypothesis of the other.
conclusions: For every x,t∈ℝ, the function τ ↦ q(x+cτ,τ) has real derivative 0 at τ=t.
If p is differentiable everywhere, then for every x,t∈ℝ there exist qt,qx∈ℝ such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative qt at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative qx at x, and qt+c·qx=0.

If p is interval integrable on every real interval with respect to μ, then all of the following hold: for every a,b,t∈ℝ, x ↦ q(x,t) is interval integrable from a to b; for every x,s,t∈ℝ, τ ↦ c·q(x,τ) is interval integrable from s to t; and for every a,b,s,t∈ℝ, ∫_a^b q(x,t) dμ(x) − ∫_a^b q(x,s) dμ(x) = ∫_s^t [c·q(a,τ) − c·q(b,τ)] dμ(τ), with all integrals oriented.
mathematical_definitions: All scalar and state spaces in the target are ℝ with their real algebraic structures and usual topology induced by |x−y|. The generic vector-space parameters of the local definitions are specialized to ℝ.
The translated profile is q(x,t)=p(x−ct), and the flux is F(z)=cz.
Having derivative v at r means having an actual ordinary real derivative equal to v at r; for real-valued f, this is the limit of (f(r+h)−f(r))/h as nonzero h tends to zero.
Differentiable ℝ p means p is differentiable at every real point, without requiring its derivative to be continuous.
Write μ for the fixed measure Real.measureSpace.volume. Interval integrability from a to b means measure-theoretic integrability on both (a,b] and (b,a] with respect to μ.
The notation ∫_a^b f dμ means ∫_(a,b] f dμ − ∫_(b,a] f dμ. It is an oriented measure-theoretic interval integral.

LocalDef001 expresses everywhere existence of the two coordinate partial derivatives together with q_t+cq_x=0. LocalDef002 expresses spatial integrability, temporal flux integrability, and the displayed finite-interval balance identity.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real-valued profile p on the whole real line and every real constant c, let q(x,t)=p(x−ct). The conjunction of five assertions holds: q agrees with p at time zero; q(x+ct,t)=p(x) for every real x,t; every characteristic trace τ ↦ q(x+cτ,τ) has derivative zero at every real time; if p is differentiable everywhere, both coordinate partial derivatives of q exist everywhere and satisfy q_t+cq_x=0; and if p is integrable on every real interval with respect to the specified real volume measure μ, every spatial slice of q and every temporal trace of its linear flux cq are interval integrable, and the change between times s and t of the oriented spatial integral over a to b equals the oriented temporal integral from s to t of the flux at a minus the flux at b. All spatial and temporal endpoints are arbitrary real numbers.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The target concerns real-valued profiles only, although the local definitions admit general real normed vector spaces.
The spatial and temporal domains are all of ℝ. There is no restriction to nonnegative time, no bounded spatial domain and no imposed ordering of interval endpoints.
The speed is a constant real number and may be positive, negative or zero.

The first three clauses require no continuity, measurability or differentiability of p. The characteristic trace is constant by the second clause, so its differentiability does not imply existence of either coordinate partial derivative of q.

For a profile that is not differentiable everywhere, the fourth implication is vacuous. For a profile that fails the universal interval-integrability assumption, the fifth implication is vacuous. The unconditional clauses still apply.

The differential clause requires actual coordinate derivatives, avoiding equations involving merely default values of a total derivative operator. It does not explicitly require joint differentiability or continuity of the partial derivatives.
The integrability hypothesis concerns every finite interval, not integrability on the entire real line. No decay, compact support or finite total mass is required.
For equal spatial endpoints or equal temporal endpoints, the balance identity reduces to a zero identity. Its universal quantification also includes all nondegenerate intervals.
When c=0, q(x,t)=p(x) and the flux vanishes. The temporal flux integrability requirement is then automatic, while spatial integrability remains part of the final conclusion.
The proposition verifies the explicitly defined q. It does not assert uniqueness, classify all solutions, or quantify over an arbitrary solution of the differential or integral equation.

The integral predicate explicitly encodes a finite-interval balance law and trace integrability. It does not explicitly encode a test-function formulation, entropy conditions or an almost-everywhere differential equation.
The partial derivative witnesses occur separately at each point; no globally quantified witness functions or explicit formulas for the derivatives are included.
ambiguities: Real.measureSpace is displayed only as inferInstance. The packet fixes its volume measure syntactically but does not expand its construction or normalization. The translation therefore denotes this exact measure by μ; identifying it explicitly with normalized Lebesgue measure requires information beyond the displayed body.
